Subject: RE: Crestline DPA (initial redline) + subprocessor inventory — annotated comments & runbook

Team / Laura — attaching our annotated redline (RI_Annotated_DPA_Redline_v1_neha.pdf) and a short execution runbook below. High-level comments:

Key redline suggestions:
- Transfers: Insert EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) by reference in the transfer clause and add a fall-back that allows us to rely on SCCs supplemented by technical/organizational safeguards (example language included in the PDF). For any subprocessor hosting in the EU/UK, require written confirmation that SCCs are in place.
- Subprocessor notice: we propose 10 days’ prior notice for material changes and an expedited 24–72 hour notification window for emergency disclosures (e.g., legal process). Crestline’s suggested 10-day notice is OK but we’ll ask to exclude routine maintenance updates from the formal notice cadence.
- Retention: propose tiered retention limits (logs/telemetry 90 days; aggregated analytics 3 years; user-submitted patient metadata — configurable per account with default 7 years unless regulated retention requires otherwise).
- PHI/Regulated data: need confirmation. If Crestline intends to route PHI to Redwood, we should execute a BA Agreement or add explicit HIPAA BA terms to the DPA.
- Evidence: Crestline asked for KMS/HSM and SOC2 evidence. We can provide SOC2 report summary and a redacted KMS architecture diagram; for HSM we will confirm HSM use on dedicated nodes. Markus — can you pull the SOC2 excerpt and KMS doc?

Execution runbook (proposed):
- Envelope 1 (DocuSign): Core DPA + Annex A (processing details) — signers: Crestline VP Legal (Laura Mitchell) -> Redwood VP Legal (Neha Kapoor) -> Redwood Director Accounts (Vanessa Ortiz)
- Envelope 2 (DocuSign): Subprocessor Inventory acknowledgement + Appendix (signers: Crestline Security Ops -> Redwood Security Ops (Markus))
- Each envelope with audit trail and signer email verification. Keep envelopes separated so subprocessor update dates are discrete.
- Deliverables after signing: a stamped copy via DocuSign, and a Drive folder with evidence items (SOC2 excerpt, KMS diagram).

I will incorporate language for SCCs and the tiered retention policy in the annotated PDF. If Crestline confirms no PHI, we can skip BA language; otherwise we’ll prepare BA text for review.

Attachments referenced: RI_Annotated_DPA_Redline_v1_neha.pdf

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor

From: Wilson & Hart LLP <privacy@wilsonhart.com>

Date: Thu, 17 May 2028 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Crestline DPA (initial redline) + subprocessor inventory — points on SCCs & retention

Neha / Vanessa — thanks for the quick turn. A few points from counsel side:

1) SCCs: Crestline requires explicit confirmation that SCCs are in effect for any transfer outside the EEA/UK. A clause by reference is ok but we need a signed link or appendix confirming which SCCs apply and where they are implemented. Please include a short schedule listing third-country subprocessors and locations.

2) Retention: Crestline’s clinical record retention window is set by state law; their ask to have a configurable retention default is acceptable but we need a clear mechanism (API or console) for a customer to set retention and for Redwood to confirm deletion. Please indicate how deletion is verified.

3) PHI: Client indicates they may route PHI in scoped workloads. If that is the case Redwood must add BA language or confirm that the DPA will operate as a BAA (including breach notification timelines aligned to health-regulation windows).

4) Subprocessor notice: Client wants explicit 10-day notice for new subprocessors that process personal data, plus a right to object within 10 days. We understand Redwood’s operational constraints; propose Redwood to commit to notice + right to object, with an expedited SME discussion to resolve objections within 10 business days.

Please send an updated redline reflecting SCC schedule and the deletion verification mechanism. We will review and return comments Wednesday next week.

Best —
Wilson & Hart LLP
privacy@wilsonhart.com

Laura / Counsel — quick summary and proposed schedule so we keep momentum:

- We accept the SCC-by-reference approach and will provide a short SCC Schedule listing current third-country subprocessors and locations. Neha will add the SCC schedule to the annotated redline by EOD Friday.
- Retention: Redwood will provide a configurable retention control in the Console (API + UI) and a deletion verification event (deletion job + console audit record). Markus will attach the SOC2 excerpt and a sample deletion audit screenshot to the Drive folder when available.
- PHI: Priyom is confirming whether the Crestline workload will include PHI. If so, we will produce BA language and an addendum for review (ETA next Tue).
- Subprocessor notice / objection: Redwood proposes 10-day notice for material new subprocessors and will include an objection process: customer raises objection within 10 days, parties escalate to SME call; if unresolved after 10 business days we fall back to pre-agreed mitigation or pausing onboarding of that subprocessor for Crestline’s tenant.

Execution: please confirm signers and PO number by Monday. Plan to send: Envelope 1 (Core DPA + Annex) on Tue 23 May; Envelope 2 (Subprocessor inventory acknowledgement) Tue 23 May (separate envelope). Both envelopes will include audit trail. DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/envelope/ABC123-Crestline-DPA

Attachments: we will upload the RI_Annotated_DPA_Redline_v1_neha.pdf and SOC2 excerpt to the shared Drive link and add the SCC schedule once finalized.
